summary: A silent turn-2 hang (send, no reply) now becomes a visible, recoverable failure. A single-shot QTimer armed per send fires after the 30s server slow-op budget + 5s margin, clears the waiting state, hides the typing indicator, and appends ONE 'send again' line. One shared _clear_waiting_state() teardown stops the watchdog on every wait-ending path (reply, failed send, connection error, disconnect), so it can never outlive its wait and fire a stray line. All headless-measurable acceptances pass under stock CPython AND on the live H22.0.400 runtime via an offscreen hython real-QTimer probe. Only the live-GUI seat (acceptance 5) is UNKNOWN — no Houdini GUI is available to this agent.

acceptance.evidence: tests/test_response_watchdog.py::test_connection_error_clears_waiting_via_shared_helper and ::test_disconnect_status_clears_waiting_via_shared_helper. chat_panel.py:_on_connection_error and _on_status_changed(False) both call _clear_waiting_state; grep confirms the two clearing lines exist in exactly ONE place (init + helper) — no third copy.

findings.claim: The watchdog budget is a named constant WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_MS = 30000 (server slow-op budget) + 5000 (margin) = 35000 ms. It is NOT imported from server.main_thread._SLOW_TIMEOUT on purpose: the panel keeps server imports lazy (chat_panel._get_server_class) to avoid import-time coupling, so the 30s is cited in a comment as the producer path instead. Drift risk: if _SLOW_TIMEOUT changes, this constant must be re-checked.
findings.anchor: python/synapse/panel/chat_panel.py (constants block near _CONTEXT_MAX_AGE_MS); server budget at python/synapse/server/main_thread.py:22 (_SLOW_TIMEOUT = 30.0)

findings.claim: The arm and the helper's stop are guarded by `if self._response_watchdog is not None`. This keeps pre-existing tests that drive _send_message / _on_response WITHOUT building the timer (no createInterface) green — the timer is only None before createInterface, which never happens in production. Regression confirmed: tests/test_chat_panel.py 85 passed/17 skipped, tests/panel/ 117 passed/89 skipped, 0 failed.

The headless test has two layers. Layer 1 (mock timer) runs under stock CPython and is the always-run acceptance evidence; it drives the fire slot as a fake clock and asserts start/stop calls + panel state. Layer 2 is a REAL single-shot QTimer that only runs under a genuine PySide (hython) — it skips under the MagicMock stub via an isActive()-is-bool discriminator (skip != pass). Runtime truth was obtained by running the same logic under hython 22.0.400 (RESULT ALL PASS).

NO_RESPONSE_LINE lives in chat_panel.py rather than send_guard.py (where the sibling *_LINE constants live) because send_guard.py is outside this mission's `touches`. Minimal-diff was kept; if a future change unifies the panel's system lines, this constant should move to send_guard.py with the family.

for_ruling.item: Live-GUI confirmation (acceptance 5) is UNKNOWN and needs a human: open a real H22 panel, send a turn 2 that the server never answers (e.g. bridge stalled), and confirm the 'No response ... send that message again' line appears and the input is usable again. The headless + hython evidence proves the logic; only the live seat is unobtained.
